title: Outdoor Den Building
strapline: Poles, tarps, pegs and teamwork — building a hideout you can actually crawl into, together.
intent: Children solve real construction problems — how to make it stand, stay up, keep the rain out — through trial, error and persistence.
Children collaborate genuinely: sharing a big physical job needs talk, negotiation, turn-taking and shared purpose.
Children develop gross-motor strength and coordination hauling, tying, propping and threading materials.
Children experience the pride and ownership of a space they made themselves and can play inside.
Children explore early physics — balance, tension, structure, waterproofing — with their whole bodies.
implementation: Offer real building materials: bamboo canes, tarpaulins, old sheets, rope, pegs, crates, and a fence, tree or A-frame to build against.
Pose the challenge and step back — 'can you make a den big enough for three of you?' — then let the problem-solving be theirs.
Resist building it for them; offer a well-timed question instead — 'what could stop it falling?' — when they're genuinely stuck.
Support the teamwork: help them hear each other, share the big jobs and negotiate, without taking over the play.
Test it together: 'will it keep the rain out?' — pour a watering can over it and let them see and fix the leaks.
Let dens live for days if space allows, so children return, improve and play out long storylines inside them.
key_questions: How will you make it stand up on its own?
What could you use to keep the rain out?
How can you all work together to lift that?
It fell down — what could you try differently?
Who is your den for, and how big does it need to be?

impact.text: Children build and construct with purpose and tell you about it.
Children create with a plan and adapt when it doesn't work.
Children play cooperatively with shared ideas, keeping the play going by negotiating.
Children run, climb, lift, carry and negotiate space and obstacles with control.
Children explore forces, materials and structure — balance, tension, waterproofing — through play.

enhancements: A den 'kit bag' of rope, pegs, clips and fabric children can fetch and manage themselves.
A waterproofing challenge with watering cans to test and improve the roof.
Fairy lights or a torch to turn a finished den into a cosy evening or storytelling hideout.
A photo record of each den so children can recreate or improve on past builds.
Loose fabric, cushions and small-world figures to furnish and play inside the finished den.

playing_exploring: Children explore how materials behave, testing what stands, holds and shelters.
The open challenge invites children to have a go and take a risk with a big build.
active_learning: Children persist through collapses and setbacks to get the den standing.
The pride of a finished, playable den drives sustained effort and return visits.
creating_thinking: Children plan their structure, predict problems and adapt their approach when it fails.
They generate solutions to real construction problems and test their ideas.
